claims.text: Case 1 is a reported 57-year-old man transplanted in 2006 for primary FSGS, with basiliximab induction and prednisolone/CsA/AZA maintenance. Posttransplant diabetes developed within one year; there were no rejections and baseline graft function was stable (mean creatinine 1.8 ± 0.9 mg/dl). Seven years posttransplant, recurrent left great-toe infection with pus failed antibiotics; CsA C0 was 180.2 ng/ml. Debridement, pus culture and skin biopsy identified dematiaceous fungi/phaeohypomycosis. A three-year oral itraconazole course was associated with recurrence of symptoms, followed by improvement without other recurrence. In 2024 diabetic-nephropathy graft failure caused end-stage kidney disease and initiation of hemodialysis; Table 1 describes graft loss at 18 years. The source explicitly says none of the six were farmers or had trauma history; all received oral itraconazole 200 mg twice daily with calcineurin/liver monitoring, and no study mortality was reported. Case-header age is not converted to age at transplant or infection.

claims.text: Case 4 is a reported 44-year-old man with probable chronic pyelonephritis and live-related ABO-compatible transplant in 2015. Graft function remained stable (mean creatinine 1.3 ± 0.6 mg/dl), with no other reported complications. claims.text: Case 5 is a reported 55-year-old man with unknown native kidney disease and live-related ABO-incompatible transplant in 2015. Rituximab/three plasmapheresis sessions were used for desensitization and basiliximab for induction. Prednisolone and initial MPA were documented; MPA stopped within four months because of persistent leucopenia. Body CsA versus table Tac maintenance remains unresolved. A nonpruritic maculopapular rash over both legs developed at 5 months in body versus 0.58 years in Table 1; the exact clock and table five-year recurrence attribution are unresolved. Skin biopsy was suggestive of phaeohypomyosis, with histiocytic aggregates, no appreciable epithelioid granulomas, fibrotic cyst wall/suppuration and GMS-highlighted hyphae in Figure 1d–f. Tac Co was 6.9 ng/ml. Six months of oral itraconazole and monitored therapy was followed by clinical improvement and stable graft function (mean creatinine 1.48 ± 0.3 mg/dl). The source explicitly says none of the six were farmers or had trauma history; all received oral itraconazole 200 mg twice daily with calcineurin/liver monitoring, and no study mortality was reported. Case-header age is not converted to age at transplant or infection.
